gloss: heart and soul; one's utmost energy

definitions.gloss: heart and soul; one's utmost energy
definitions.explanation: The whole of a person's mental and physical energy, thought of as something poured into a long undertaking. Used almost exclusively in the set phrase {心血|しんけつ}を{注|そそ}ぐ.

examples.japanese: {研究|けんきゅう}に{心血|しんけつ}を{注|そそ}いだ。
examples.english: He poured his heart and soul into his research.

examples.japanese: この{作品|さくひん}は{父|ちち}が{心血|しんけつ}を{注|そそ}いで{完成|かんせい}させたものだ。
examples.english: This work is one my father completed by pouring his whole self into it.

examples.japanese: {十年|じゅうねん}にわたって{心血|しんけつ}を{注|そそ}いできた{計画|けいかく}が、{予算|よさん}{不足|ぶそく}で{中止|ちゅうし}になった。
examples.english: The project she had devoted herself to for ten years was cancelled for lack of funds.

notes:
{心|しん} (heart, mind) + {血|けつ} (blood): the image is of giving both spirit and lifeblood.

USAGE:
Almost never used alone. The phrase {心血|しんけつ}を{注|そそ}ぐ takes に for the object of the effort ({作品|さくひん}に{心血|しんけつ}を{注|そそ}ぐ), and fits work carried on over years rather than a single burst of effort. Written and somewhat elevated in tone.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {全力|ぜんりょく}を{尽|つ}くす: to do one's very best — neutral, and usable of a short effort
- {精魂|せいこん}を{込|こ}める: to put one's soul into — similar in weight, focused on craftsmanship
- {丹精|たんせい}を{込|こ}める: to work with painstaking care — typically of gardening or handiwork
